quests.instruction: Find the link where a word ending in two consonants joins a vowel
quests.textToSpeak: I'll send the minutes out after the meeting
quests.hint: The consonant pile at the end of one word does not stop it linking. Which word?
quests.explanation: Meeting follow-ups are said at speed, so 'minutes out' becomes one stretch: the /ts/ at the end of 'minutes' hands its /s/ to the /aʊ/ of 'out'. 'Out after' links too, but through a single /t/.
quests.flowRule: Linking after consonant clusters: When a word ends in two or three consonants, the last one still connects into a following vowel, so the ending is carried across the boundary smoothly.

quests.instruction: Which link has a light /w/ glide between two vowels?
quests.textToSpeak: Sam will walk us through it then answer questions
quests.hint: Which vowel-to-vowel boundary starts from rounded lips?
quests.explanation: In a meeting, 'through it' is run together: the rounded /uː/ of 'through' slides into the /ɪ/ of 'it' with a faint /w/. 'Walk us' and 'then answer' are consonant-to-vowel links, so they are not the answer.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Linking with a /w/ glide: After vowels made with rounded lips (/uː/, /əʊ/, /aʊ/), many speakers slide through a light /w/ before the next vowel. It is a natural transition, not a written letter, and it is subtle.

quests.instruction: Find the first place where one word runs into the next
quests.textToSpeak: we'll run out of time if we keep talking
quests.hint: Say the sentence at normal speed and mark each place where a consonant runs into a vowel. Take the first.
quests.explanation: A chair watching the clock says this fast. The /n/ of 'run' flows into the /aʊ/ of 'out', and 'out of' follows through /t/, so the front of the sentence is one chain.
quests.flowRule: Thought groups: Fluent speakers connect words across a whole phrase, so one sentence can contain several links. The instruction tells you which one to find; listen to the sounds on each side of a boundary.

quests.instruction: Find the link that slides through a 'w' sound
quests.textToSpeak: I'll put you through in a moment
quests.hint: 'Put you' is not a vowel link. Find the pair with a vowel on both sides.
quests.explanation: Putting a caller through is routine, so it comes out in one run. The /uː/ of 'through' relaxes into the /ɪ/ of 'in' with a faint /w/. 'In a' is the consonant-to-vowel link that follows.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Linking with a /w/ glide: After vowels made with rounded lips (/uː/, /əʊ/, /aʊ/), many speakers slide through a light /w/ before the next vowel. It is a natural transition, not a written letter, and it is subtle.

quests.instruction: Which is the last connection in this sentence?
quests.textToSpeak: I'm afraid he's in a meeting at the moment
quests.hint: Start from the right and stop at the first consonant-to-vowel join.
quests.explanation: Receptionists say this on a loop, so it runs in one breath. The /ŋ/ of 'meeting' flows into the weak /ət/ of 'at', right before the stress lands on 'moment'. 'He's in' and 'in a' come first.
quests.flowRule: Thought groups: Fluent speakers connect words across a whole phrase, so one sentence can contain several links. The instruction tells you which one to find; listen to the sounds on each side of a boundary.

quests.instruction: Which is the second link in this sentence?
quests.textToSpeak: I'll make a note of that and call you back
quests.hint: Say it at normal speed. After the first link, the next one is the answer.
quests.explanation: 'Make a', 'note of' and 'that and' each put a small word on the end of a bigger one. The /t/ of 'note' lands on the weak /əv/, so the pair is heard as one beat. 'Call you back' has no vowel link.
quests.flowRule: Reduced forms: Unstressed to, and, of, at, it, us and a shrink to /tə/, /ən/, /əv/, /ət/, /ɪt/, /əs/ and /ə/, so a link into one of them sounds like the end of the word before it.

quests.instruction: Find the link that runs on a hum (m, n or ng)
quests.textToSpeak: do you have this in a larger size
quests.hint: Only a few word endings use the nose. Find one that is followed by a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: Shop assistants hear this question all day. The /n/ of 'in' keeps the voice humming into the weak /ə/ of 'a'. 'This in' is the other link, through /s/.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking (nasals): A word ending in /m/ or /n/ keeps your voice running, so the nasal sound flows directly into a following vowel with no gap.

quests.instruction: Find the link carried by a 'ch' or 'j' sound
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to exchange it for a different colour
quests.hint: Listen for a 'ch' or 'j' sound that does not stop, but slides into the next word.
quests.explanation: The /dʒ/ at the end of 'exchange' is released straight into the vowel of 'it'. 'For a' is the other link, through an /r/ that rhotic speakers always pronounce. Returns desks hear this phrase a lot, so it comes out fast.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking (affricates): The 'ch' sound /tʃ/ and the 'j' sound /dʒ/ at the end of a word are released directly into the next vowel instead of being cut off.

quests.instruction: Find the link where a written r returns before a vowel
quests.textToSpeak: is there a discount if I buy two
quests.hint: Look for a word spelled with 're' just before a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: 'There' ends in a written re, a final /r/ that links into the weak /ə/ of 'a'. In non-rhotic accents the /r/ appears here but not in 'there now'. 'Discount if' and 'if I' link through other sounds.
quests.flowRule: Linking /r/ (accent-dependent): In rhotic accents (most of North America, Scotland, Ireland) a word-final r is always pronounced, so it simply connects to a following vowel. In non-rhotic accents (for example most of England, Australia, New Zealand) the r is silent before a consonant or a pause but usually returns before a vowel, as in 'far away'. Either way, the two words connect.

quests.instruction: Which link carries a linking /r/?

quests.hint: Look for a word ending in -er before a vowel.
quests.explanation: 'Starter' ends in a written r, so rhotic speakers say the /r/ before 'and' as always, and non-rhotic speakers bring it back there. 'Like a' is the other link, through /k/. A restaurant order has a steady rhythm.

quests.instruction: Which link has a nasal sound meeting a vowel?

quests.explanation: Diet and allergy questions are said quickly. The /n/ of 'vegetarian' runs into the weak /ɔː/ of 'or', and 'does it' follows through /z/. The nasal link is the first.

quests.instruction: Find the link carried by the sound /l/
quests.textToSpeak: could we get the bill as soon as possible
quests.hint: Which boundary has /l/ on the left and a vowel on the right?
quests.explanation: Asking for the bill is polite and quick. The dark /l/ of 'bill' stays on the tongue as the weak /əz/ of 'as' begins. 'Soon as' links through /n/ and sits inside the set phrase 'as soon as'.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking (/l/): A word-final /l/ stays voiced and slides into the vowel of the next word, so the two words sound like one continuous stretch.

quests.instruction: Which link carries the past-tense ending?
quests.textToSpeak: I booked a double room for two nights under Smith
quests.hint: A /t/ or /d/ hides at the end of a past verb. Which one lands on a vowel?
quests.explanation: At check-in, 'booked a' is said as one beat: the /t/ of 'booked' lands on the weak /ə/ of 'a' and signals the past tense. 'Nights under' is the other link, through /s/.
quests.flowRule: Past-tense endings link too: A final -ed (/t/ or /d/) joins a following vowel, which also keeps the past-tense signal audible.

quests.instruction: Which pair is joined by a nasal sound?

quests.explanation: Hotel guests ask this in one breath. The lips close for the /m/ of 'time' and the voice carries into the /ɪ/ of 'is'. 'Breakfast and' and 'check out' link through stops.
quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking (nasals): A word ending in /m/ or /n/ keeps your voice running, so the nasal sound flows directly into a following vowel with no gap.

quests.hint: Look for a word that ends in a written r or re before a vowel.
quests.explanation: 'Here' ends in a final /r/ that links into the /ʌ/ of 'until'. In non-rhotic accents this is the only place the r reappears. 'Is it' and 'leave our' are other links, through /z/ and /v/.

quests.instruction: Find the link carried by a 'th' sound

quests.flowRule: Consonant-to-Vowel Linking (/θ/ and /ð/): The 'th' sounds at the end of a word stay in the airflow and connect to a following vowel instead of stopping.

quests.instruction: Which link has a light /j/ ('y') glide between two vowels?

quests.explanation: In an interview answer, a number runs into a noun: the /iː/ of 'three' slides into the vowel of 'offices' with a faint /j/. The other links in the sentence all join a consonant to a vowel.
quests.flowRule: Vowel-to-Vowel Linking with a /j/ glide: After vowels made with the tongue high and forward (/iː/, /eɪ/, /aɪ/, /ɔɪ/), many speakers slide through a light /j/ ('y') before the next vowel. It is a natural transition, not a written letter, and it is subtle.

quests.instruction: Which link carries a consonant cluster?
